documents.title: CU Committee Report: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Education and Pedagogy
documents.summary: The 2023 university-wide committee report recommends a flexible framework with three instructor-chosen approaches to GAI (prohibit, allow with attribution, encourage) tied to learning outcomes. It also advises on detectors, accessibility, privacy, instructor use of GAI, and administrative actions, including that the Code of Academic Integrity say student use is only allowed when expressly permitted.

documents.title: AI & Academic Integrity
documents.summary: The Center for Teaching Innovation guidance tells instructors to communicate AI policy in the syllabus and offers four sample course statements. It also sets out a procedure for suspected violations (inquiry, objective evidence, clear and convincing standard), citation advice, and a recommendation not to use AI detectors.
documents.stance_why: The page does not set one rule; it supplies sample statements ('AI-FREE', 'AS-UA', 'ANY-AI-UA', 'AS') for instructors to adapt, so the stance is delegates and the four templates are the tiers.
